query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using spark plasma sintering (SPS) with a rapid heat treatment schedule will induce an in situ dual-phase microstructure in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that incorporates a ductile secondary phase to improve structural integrity without significantly degrading the caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: A homogeneous, single-phase (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy exhibiting a large caloric response but poor mechanical integrity with a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Apply SPS consolidation with a rapid heat treatment protocol during sintering to control phase formation.
generation.conditions: Processing and subsequent testing under applied magnetic fields of approximately 2 T and pressure fields up to around 500 MPa, near-room temperature conditions (approximately 20–50 °C), and under cyclic mechanical loading similar to device operation.
generation.structural_mediator: A dual-phase microstructure in which fine, ductile secondary phase particles are dispersed within the primary caloric-active phase.
generation.mechanism: The rapid heat treatment during SPS promotes controlled phase separation, resulting in the formation of a reinforcing ductile phase that acts as an internal binder to arrest crack propagation. Meanwhile, the primary phase responsible for the large caloric effect is maintained, thereby preserving the functional performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The processed alloy is expected to exhibit a significant increase in mechanical integrity evidenced by enhanced compressive strength (approaching or exceeding 150–220 MPa as seen with epoxy composites) and improved crack resistance, while the caloric response is maintained within roughly 10% of its original value.
generation.baseline: The unchanged alloy features a high caloric response but suffers from poor structural integrity and cracking under similar applied-field conditions.
generation.boundary: These improvements are expected under the specified testing conditions (applied magnetic field ~2 T, pressure up to ~500 MPa, near-room temperature, and cyclic loading). The effectiveness outside these regimes (e.g., at very high or low temperatures or extreme loading rates) remains untested.
generation.uncertainty: The exact volume fraction, morphology, and distribution of the ductile secondary phase and its precise quantitative impact on both caloric and mechanical properties need to be experimentally determined. There is also uncertainty regarding any potential minor trade-off in caloric performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy samples using the SPS method with a rapid heat treatment schedule and compare them with control samples processed via conventional methods. Characterize the microstructure to confirm dual-phase formation and perform mechanical and caloric testing under an applied magnetic field (~2 T) and pressure (up to ~500 MPa) at near-room temperature with cyclic loading.
measurements: Compressive strength and fatigue crack propagation tests
Caloric effect quantification under applied magnetic and pressure fields
Microstructural analysis (SEM/TEM) to assess phase distribution and morphology
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SPS-processed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., compressive strength and reduced cracking) without a drop of more than about 10% in the caloric response compared to conventionally processed samples, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

chosen.technique: spark plasma sintering with a rapid heat treatment schedule aimed at forming an in situ dual-phase microstructure that couples the caloric phase with a ductile, reinforcing secondary phase
chosen.conditions: Under applied magnetic fields (~2 T) and pressure fields (up to ~500 MPa) at near-room temperature with cyclic mechanical loading; ensuring that the composition remains rare-earth free
chosen.why: This intervention directly targets the unresolved coexistence of robust structural integrity and high caloric response by optimizing processing conditions to tailor the microstructure. It builds upon established SPS techniques in materials science to achieve a dual-phase architecture that provides enhanced toughness without sacrificing functional caloric performance. Prior work with epoxy and low-melting-indium composites showed that ‘partial’ solutions (improving one metric at the expense of another) can be overcome by a unified, processing-driven strategy that addresses both issues simultaneously.
